packet.exact_semantic_question: What monitoring frequencies do opaque LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE values (e.g. 05/WK, 01/07, 01/01) establish?
packet.relation_contract: frequency codes must be interpreted for monitoring obligations

candidate_interpretations.description: Codes encode a sample count and period denominator (e.g. 05/WK = five samples per week; 01/07 = one sample per seven-day period; 02/30 = two samples per thirty-day period; 01/90 = one sample per ninety-day period). Supported only by permit-document pairing, not by any code legend in the workspace.
Code 99/99 denotes continuous totalizing-meter flow monitoring rather than discrete sample collection on a calendar schedule.
Code 09/99 marks WET retest reporting parameters whose permit narrative describes conditional retesting after test failure, not a fixed calendar sampling interval.
Opaque codes cannot be assigned reusable monitoring-frequency semantics from workspace sources alone because no document names the codes or defines the NN/XX grammar.

proposal.remaining_uncertainty: No reusable code-to-frequency mapping is admissible from workspace sources. Candidate positive interpretations (periodic_count_per_period, continuous_metering, event_driven_retest) rest on permit-document-to-CSV correlation or single-permit context without a published code legend. Admitting any of them as World truth would require SOURCE_ESTABLISHED grounding that the packet does not provide.

refinement.why_necessary: Retrieved evidence shows LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE values serve materially different obligation types. Most codes (05/WK, 01/07, 01/01, 02/07, 02/30, 01/90) align with calendar-period sampling frequencies stated in permit Part I tables when joined by permit and parameter. Code 99/99 appears only for continuous totalizing-meter flow, which is not a sample-count-per-period obligation. Code 09/99 appears only on WET retest parameter rows whose permit narrative describes conditional retesting after test failure rather than a fixed calendar schedule. Treating all codes as one homogeneous 'monitoring frequency' question obscures these distinct semantic contracts.
